newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PM says trade gap economy's main problem.
newsitem.headline: Czech PM says trade gap economy's main problem.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said on Tuesday the main problem facing the country's economy was a widening trade deficit, but he ruled out a devaluation of the crown to help the situation.
Klaus added in a speech to business leaders at the Zofin Forum that he saw no fundamental changes to the exchange rate of the crown "in the future".

"I am only reminding you that the cure for our trade deficit cannot be any devaluation of the crown and fortunately the government, the central bank and the majority of analysts agree with this," Klaus said.

The Czech trade deficit, spurred by imports of raw materials and machinery needed for industrial restructuring, widened to a record 160.3 billion crowns for the whole of 1996, up from 95.7 billion the previous year.
The deficit is forecast to grow even further in 1997, to around 210-220 billion crowns.

With regard to the crown's current exchange rate, Klaus said: "The rate through the year, moved in the short term more often than in the past but -- precisely as we expected -- there was no fundamnetal change. And there should not be even in the future."

The currency, buoyed by a wave of over 40 billion crowns worth of crown-denomiated Eurobonds issued since the beginning of the year, hit a record high of +5.51 percent against the mid-point of its dollar/mark basket last month.

After rising some three percent against basket parity in January and the beginning of February, the crown then retreated to around +1.0 percent on comments by the central bank that the currency was overvalued and interest rates could be cut.
No moves were actually taken by the central bank, and the currnecy has since crept back up to be fixed by the central bank at +2.68 percent on Tuesday.
